Il rendimento del Treasury USA a 10 anni è calato del 4,7% a 4,91%. audio_narrative_it.text: Nikkei ha registrato un ribasso del 7,7% nella settimana, Shanghai è in calo del 2,8% e Hang Seng è diminuito del 5,2%.

audio_narrative_it.title: Macro ed Economia
audio_narrative_it.text: L'economia giapponese si è contratta per la prima volta in un anno, contribuendo al sell‑off asiatico. Warsh ha evidenziato che il boom dell'IA potrebbe sostenere una crescita più alta negli USA, ma non è bastato a invertire il sentiment. Le compagnie aeree hanno subito pressione a causa della scadenza delle coperture carburante, spingendo il prezzo del petrolio al ribasso nonostante l'escalation USA‑Iran. Il sentiment è stato risk‑off per tutta la settimana, partendo in territorio negativo e chiudendo ancora in zona neutra.

audio_narrative_it.title: Criptovalute
audio_narrative_it.text: Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si muove al rialzo del 3,8%, mantenendosi sopra gli ottantamila dollari. Il flusso ETF cumulativo della settimana è stato di -445,7 milioni di dollari, rispetto a +986,7 milioni la settimana precedente, una variazione di -1,432,4 milioni. L’ultimo flusso giornaliero, riferito a venerdì, è stato di +3,8 milioni. Ethereum cresce del 3,8%, raggiungendo i duemilatrecentounomila dollari. Solana aumenta del 2,9%, arrivando a sessantunodue dollari. BNB sale del 4,1%, arrivando a cinquecentotrentotto dollari. Il sentiment di mercato è “Extreme Fear”, con un indice di 11, suggerendo cautela agli investitori. In sintesi, Bitcoin e gli altcoins principali mostrano una crescita moderata, ma gli ETF registrano un netto negativo, mentre il sentiment rimane molto negativo, indicando potenziali rischi per chi entra ora.

audio_narrative_en.title: Opening
audio_narrative_en.text: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. Today we recap the just concluded week in the markets.

audio_narrative_en.title: Wall Street
audio_narrative_en.text: The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39, down 8.6% for the week, Nasdaq at 22,618 with a 10.0% decline, and Dow Jones at 48,147, down 8.0%. The VIX rose 86%, indicating high volatility. Gold fell 9.5% to $3,515.40 per ounce. Brent lost 6.2% at $89.95 per barrel. The U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield fell 4.7% to 4.91%. The main driver was the strong negative impact of falling oil prices, amplified by the airline hedging crisis.

audio_narrative_en.title: Europe
audio_narrative_en.text: The STOXX 600 fell 5.9% for the week, FTSE MIB lost 6.1%, and the 10‑year BTP remained stable around 4.68%.

audio_narrative_en.title: Asian Markets
audio_narrative_en.text: The Nikkei fell 7.7% for the week, Shanghai down 2.8%, and Hang Seng dropped 5.2%.

audio_narrative_en.title: Macroeconomics
audio_narrative_en.text: The Japanese economy contracted for the first time in a year, contributing to the Asian sell‑off. Warsh noted that the AI boom could support higher growth in the U.S., but it was not enough to reverse sentiment. Airlines faced pressure due to the expiration of fuel hedges, pushing oil prices lower despite the U.S.–Iran escalation. Sentiment was risk‑off all week, starting negative and ending still in neutral territory.

audio_narrative_en.title: Cryptocurrencies
audio_narrative_en.text: Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is up 3.8%, staying above $80,000. The cumulative ETF flow for the week was $-445.7 million, versus $986.7 million the previous week, a change of $-1,432.4 million. The latest daily flow, for Friday, was $3.8 million. Ethereum rises 3.8%, reaching $2,301,000. Solana increases 2.9%, reaching $62.12. BNB rises 4.1%, reaching $538. The market sentiment is "Extreme Fear", with an index of 11, suggesting caution for investors. In summary, Bitcoin and the main altcoins show moderate growth, but ETFs register a net negative, while sentiment remains very negative, indicating potential risks for those entering now.

audio_narrative_en.title: Closing
audio_narrative_en.text: For deeper coverage of today’s topics, find the full articles in the Spotlight Stories section on our platform. A greeting from Price Alert
